Rashi on Niddah 60a:10:1.hebrew: לפיכך דרבן שמעון למה לי - כיון דתנא תולה בה, פשיטא דהיא מתוקנת וזו מקולקלת:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:10:1.english: Why do I need the "therefore" of Rabban Shimon - Since [the tanna] taught that she attributes [the stain] to her, it is obvious that she is unimpaired and this one is impaired.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:12:1.hebrew: שהלכו בשני שבילין - ולא ידענא הי להאי על, והי להאי על:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:12:1.english: Who walked on two paths - And we do not know which one entered this [path], and which one entered that [path].

Rashi on Niddah 60a:12:2.hebrew: באנו למחלוקת - לרבן שמעון, דאמר תולין כתם בשומרת יום, הכא נמי תולין שביל טמא באדם טמא וטהור בטהור; ולרבי, שניהם טמאים:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:12:2.english: We have arrived at the dispute - According to Rabban Shimon, who says that we attribute a stain to a woman who observes a day [for a day], here too, we attribute the impure path to the impure person, and the pure [path] to the pure [person]; and according to Rabbi, both of them are impure.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:13:1.english: Rabbi said only this far - That the second [woman] is ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:13:2.hebrew: אלא משום דכי הדדי נינהו - שתיהן היו בחזקת טהרה: השומרת יום בשני שלה ראויה לטבול כל שעה שתרצה, כיון שספרה שעה אחת. הילכך, אין כאן טומאה שתוכל לתלות בה יותר מזאת, לפיכך שתיהן טמאות. אבל הכא, דטמא הוא, מאי נפקא ליה מינה אי תלית ביה? הילכך, אפילו לרבי תלינן:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:13:2.english: Rather, because they are like each other - Both of them had a presumption of purity: the woman who observes a day [for a day], on her second day, is fit to immerse at any time she wishes, once she has counted one hour. Therefore, there is no [established] impurity here that you could attribute [the stain] to her more than to this [other woman]; therefore, both of them are impure. But here, where he is [already] impure, what difference does it make to him if you attribute [the impure path] to him? Therefore, even according to Rabbi, we attribute [it to him].

Rashi on Niddah 60a:14:1.hebrew: ורב חסדא אמר סוף סוף - הך שומרת יום טבילה היא בעיא, הילכך טמאה הואי, ואפילו הכי קאמר רבי: לא תלינן בה:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:14:1.english: And Rav Ḥisda said: Ultimately - This woman observing a day [for a day] requires immersion; therefore, she was ritually impure, and even so, Rabbi says we do not attribute [the stain] to her.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:1.hebrew: איתמר נמי - כרב אדא, דאמר: אפילו לרבי תלינן שביל טמא בטמא. וכמדומה לי דלא גרס נמי:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:1.english: It was also stated - [This is] in accordance with Rav Adda, who said that even according to Rabbi, we attribute the impure path to the impure [person]. And it seems to me that one should not read "also".

Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:2.hebrew: טמא וטהור - או אפילו טהור ותלוי שהלכו כו', תולה טהור את שביל טמא בתלוי:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:2.english: An impure person and a pure person - [In the case of] "Or even a pure person and one of uncertain status who walked, etc.," the pure person attributes the impure path to the one of uncertain status.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:3.hebrew: לדברי הכל - ואפילו לרבי. וכדאמרינן: דהתם הוא דכי הדדי נינהו, אבל הכא, דתלוי טמא מספק וטהור טהור גמור, תולין טומאה בתלוי:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:15:3.english: According to everyone - And even according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]. And as we said: It is [only] there that they are like each other, but here, where the one in suspense is impure due to uncertainty and the pure one is completely pure, we attribute the impurity to the one in suspense.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:16:1.hebrew: כתם בכתם - השאילה חלוקה לבעלת הכתם, ואח"כ לבשתה היא, מהו שתתלה בראשונה להיות היא טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:16:1.english: A stain to a stain - [If a woman] lent her tunic to a woman [who was impure due to] a stain, and afterward she [the owner] wore it [and found a stain upon it], what is [the ruling as to whether] she may attribute [the stain] to the first [woman], so that she [herself] will be pure?

Rashi on Niddah 60a:17:1.english: [The] woman who observes a day for a day saw [blood] yesterday from her body.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:18:1.english: She may not attribute [it] - And both of them are ritually impure.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:19:1.hebrew: לפי שאין תולין - דמעלמא אתי לה טומאת כתם קמא, ולא בחזקת רואה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:19:1.english: Because one does not attribute - For the impurity of the first stain came to her from an external source, and she is not presumed to be one who sees [blood from her body].

Rashi on Niddah 60a:1:1.english: Who sees - That she is an adult, and we know about her that she has already seen [blood].

Rashi on Niddah 60a:22:1.hebrew: בשני שלה - אינה תולה, דמקלקלה לה, שמארכת ימי טומאת כתמה יום אחד. אבל ביום ראשון, שלבשה חלוק זה ביום ראשון (לכתמה הראשון), תולה, דלא מקלקלה לה מידי:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:22:1.english: On her second [day] - She may not attribute [the stain to her], because she disadvantages her, as she extends the days of impurity of her stain by one day. But on the first day, when she wore this garment on the first day (of her first stain), she may attribute [the stain to her], as she does not disadvantage her at all.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:3:1.english: Fit to see - That the days of youth have arrived.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:4:1.hebrew: ותסברא רבי מאיר לחומרא הוא - דתימא דלתנא קמא אפילו אינה ראויה, ותשמע מינה דלתרוייהו לא בעינן שראתה כבר? והא תניא דרבי מאיר לקולא, מכלל דלת"ק לא סגי בראויה לראות עד שתהא רואה ממש:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:4:1.english: And do you think that Rabbi Meir is [ruling] to be stringent - That you would say that according to the First Tanna, even [if she is] not fit [to see blood she may attribute the stain to her], and you would infer from this that according to both of them we do not require that she has already seen [blood]? And yet it is taught that Rabbi Meir is [ruling] to be lenient, which implies that according to the First Tanna it is not sufficient [that she is] fit to see, until she is actually seeing [blood].

Rashi on Niddah 60a:5:1.english: And we object: Rather, that is difficult - The first [baraita], which implies that Rabbi Meir is stringent.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:5:2.hebrew: תריץ הכי כו' - וברייתא דקתני אינה תולה בנכרית, לת"ק הכי קאמר: אינה תולה בנכרית הראויה לראות, אלא אם כן רואה. ר' מאיר אומר: תולה. ותרוייהו מתניתא חדא מילתא אמרי, ורב דאמר כתנא קמא דתרוייהו:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:5:2.english: Resolve it like this, etc. - And the baraita that taught, "She does not attribute to a gentile woman," according to the First Tanna, this is what it means: She does not attribute [the stain] to a gentile woman who is fit to see, unless she [actually] sees [blood]. Rabbi Meir says: She attributes [it]. And both baraitot say the same thing, and Rav, who said [that she does not attribute], stated [his ruling] in accordance with the First Tanna of both of them.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:6:1.hebrew: בשני שלה - אם השאילתה לשומרת יום בשני שלה, תולה בה. ואף על גב דלא הוחזקה רואה היום, כיון דמעיינה פתוח תולה בה. ואע"ג דמקלקלה לה פורתא, דצריכה לשמור יום המחרת, כיון דטמאה השתא:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:6:1.english: On her second [day] - If she lent it to a woman observing a day [for a day] on her second day, she may attribute [the stain] to her. And even though she is not presumed to see [blood] today, since her source is open, she may attribute [it] to her. And even though she impairs her [status] slightly, in that she must observe the following day, [she may attribute it to her] since she is [already] impure now.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:1.hebrew: ובסופרת ז' - נקיים אחר זיבה, ואף ע"פ שמקלקלה הרבה, שסתרה כל ימי ספירתה וצריכה לספור ז' נקיים, הואיל ועכשיו טמאה, תולה בה:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:1.english: And to a woman counting seven - [Seven] clean [days] after zivah. And even though she ruins her [status] greatly, in that she invalidates all the days of her counting and must count seven clean [days], since she is now impure, she attributes [the stain] to her.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:2.hebrew: וחברתה מקולקלת - שומרת יום צריכה עוד לשמור שלישי בשביל כתם זה, ואם סופרת היא, סותרת כל שלפניה:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:2.english: And her companion is ruined - A woman observing a day [against a day] must observe yet a third [day] on account of this stain, and if she is [a woman] counting [seven clean days], she cancels all [the days] that preceded it.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:3.hebrew: רבי אומר אינה תולה - הואיל ומקלקלה לה, מאי חזית דמקלקלת להך טפי מהך:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:7:3.english: Rabbi says she may not attribute [it] - Since [attributing it] ruins her, what did you see [to justify] ruining this one more than that one?

Rashi on Niddah 60a:8:1.english: And they agree that she may attribute [it] to a woman who observes a day for a day on her first [day] - For she does not impair [her status] at all.

Rashi on Niddah 60a:9:1.hebrew: וביושבת על דם טוהר ובבתולה שדמיה טהורין - דלא מקלקלה לה מידי, שאין לה כתם, כדאמרי' בפ' קמא (נדה דף י:), זו שירפה מצוי, ותלינן כתמה בדם בתולים:
Rashi on Niddah 60a:9:1.english: And to a woman sitting upon pure blood, and to a virgin whose blood is pure - For she does not disqualify her at all, since [the law of] a stain does not apply to her, as we say in the first chapter (Niddah 10b): "This one, her discharge is common," and we attribute her stain to hymeneal blood.

Tosafot on Niddah 60a:12:1.hebrew: טמא וטהור שהלכו בשני שבילין - הך טמא לא מיירי בטמא שספר והזה אלא שלא טבל, מדקאמר רב אדא: התם כי הדדי נינהו, הכא מאי נפקא ליה מינה — משמע דלאו דומיא דפלוגתא לעיל הוא. ובטמא שלא ספר כלל נמי לא איירי, דאפילו רבי מודה דתולה, כדאמר ושוין כו'; ואמאי קאמר רב חסדא באנו למחלוקת? אלא מיירי בטמא שספר קצת, וס"ל לרב חסדא דלרבי אפי' בספרה קצת אינה תולה. ורב אדא דקאמר מאי נפקא ליה מינה, לא קרי הפסד כיון דלא סתר הכל. והא דנקט סופרת ז' שלא טבלה, לרבותא דרשב"ג נקטיה, דאפ"ה תולה:
Tosafot on Niddah 60a:12:1.english: An impure person and a pure person who walked on two paths - This [case of an] impure person is not dealing with an impure person who counted and had [purification water] sprinkled [upon him], lacking only immersion, since Rav Adda says: "There, they are like each other; here, what difference does it make to him?"—implying that it is not similar to the dispute above. And it is also not dealing with an impure person who did not count at all, for [in that case] even Rabbi concedes that one attributes [the impurity to him], as it states: "And they agree, etc."; and [if so,] why did Rav Chisda say: "We have arrived at the dispute"? Rather, it is dealing with an impure person who counted part [of his required days], and Rav Chisda maintains that according to Rabbi, even if she counted [only] part [of her days], she may not attribute [the stain to her]. And Rav Adda, who says: "What difference does it make to him?", does not consider it a loss, since he did not forfeit everything. And that which [the baraita] formulated [the dispute regarding] "a woman counting seven who did not immerse", it formulated it to demonstrate the novelty of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel['s view], that even so, she attributes [the stain to her].

Tosafot on Niddah 60a:12:2.hebrew: באנו למחלוקת דרבי ורשב"ג - וא"ת: ורב חסדא, אמאי לא נקט מילתיה בזבה גופה, ולימא: זבה שספרה מקצתה באנו למחלוקת, כו'? וי"ל, דניחא ליה לאשמועינן דאפי' בב' שבילין מטמא, דאע"ג דהוי ספק טומאה ברה"ר. וא"ת: אם כן, מה ענין כתמים לשבילין? דאע"ג דבתרוייהו אתרע חזקת טהרה דידהו קצת, מ"מ יש לטהר יותר בשבילין משום ספק טומאה ברה"ר. וי"ל, דגבי כתם נמי איכא למימר דלא אתרע חזקתה כלל, דאיכא למתלי בחברתה כמו בשוק של טבחים; ואפ"ה לרבי אינה תולה, משום דמ"ש זו מזו, כיון ששניהם טהורין, שספרה כבר ז' ימים. הכי נמי, מאי חזית דתלינן בטמא שספר מקצת טפי מבטהור גמור? ואע"ג דאית ליה חזקה דטהרה, מיחזי כי חוכא ואטלולא; דמהאי טעמא מטמינן ב' טהורין שהלכו בשני שבילין ובאו לשאול בבת אחת, דטהורין מדינא, ומטמינא להו כי היכי דלא ליהוי כי חוכא. ואע"ג דלא דמי — דהתם אי מטהרין לתרוייהו הוי חוכא, דאי אפשר להיות ששניהם טהורין, אבל הכא אפשר דטהור הלך בטהור — מ"מ הוי חוכא, דאמאי תלינן טפי בטמא מבטהור, כדאמר לעיל גבי נשים. וא"ת: מ"ש משני קופות, דאמרינן חולין לתוך חולין נפלו? וי"ל, דהתם אינו מפסיד לחברתה בתלייתו כלום; והכא נמי, אפילו רבי מודה שתולה בנדה גמורה שלא טבלה כלל:
Tosafot on Niddah 60a:12:2.english: We have arrived at the dispute between Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel - And if you say: Why did Rav Ḥisda not state his teaching regarding a zava herself, and say: "[In the case of] a zava who counted part of her [clean days], we have arrived at the dispute, etc."? And one can say: It was preferable for him to let us know that even in [the case of] two paths [Rabbi] deems [him] impure, even though it is an uncertainty of ritual impurity in the public domain (safek tumah bi-reshut ha-rabbim). And if you say: If so, what is the connection between [blood] stains and paths? For even though in both cases their presumption of ritual purity (chezkat taharah) is somewhat impaired, nevertheless there is [more reason] to declare [a person] pure in [the case of] paths, on account of an uncertainty of impurity in the public domain! And one can say: Regarding a stain as well, one can say that her presumption [of purity] was not impaired at all, for it is possible to attribute [the stain] to her companion, just as [a woman may attribute a stain to blood from] a butchers' market; and even so, according to Rabbi she may not attribute [it], because: What is the difference between this one and that one, since both of them are pure, as she already counted seven days? So too, what did you see [to justify] attributing [the impure path] to the impure person who counted part [of his days] more than to the completely pure person? And even though he has a presumption of purity, it would appear like a mockery and a farce; for on account of this reason, we deem impure two pure people who walked on two paths and came to ask [their status] at the same time, who by strict law are pure, yet we deem them impure so that it will not be like a mockery. And even though they are not [entirely] comparable—for there, if we were to declare both of them pure it would be a mockery, as it is impossible for both of them to be pure, whereas here it is possible that the pure person walked on the pure [path]—nevertheless, it is [still] a mockery, for why should we attribute [the impure path] more to the impure person than to the pure person? Just as [Rabbi] said above regarding the women. And if you say: How is this different from [the case of] two baskets, where we say that unconsecrated produce fell into unconsecrated produce? And one can say: There, by his attributing [one to the other], he does not cause the other [basket] any loss whatsoever; and here too, even Rabbi agrees that she may attribute [a stain] to a full niddah who did not immerse at all.

Tosafot on Niddah 60a:16:1.hebrew: מהו לתלות כתם בכתם - אומר הר"י, דליכא למימר דבעי לתלות בסופרת שבעה שלא טבלה, אבל בראשון פשיטא ליה דתולה; דאם כן, מאי קאמר לקמן: מ"מ קשיא? הא איכא לשנויי: בין לרבי בין לרשב"ג, בראשון שלה איירי ברייתא! ועוד, דאליבא דרבי נמי ה"ל למבעי בראשון שלה, כיון דלא חזיא מגופה. אלא אפי' בראשון שלה מבעי ליה, ופשיט ליה דאין תולין אפי' לרשב"ג, אלא לחזיא מגופה. והשתא, לכולהו שינויי קשה לר' יהודה בר ליואי. והא דקמשני: הא והא רבי, הא בראשון שלה והא בשני שלה — הש"ס הוא דקמהדר לשנויי בכל ענין שיכול לתרץ, ולא בשיטתיה דר"י; דהא קאמר: אליבא דרבי לא תבעי לך, ואוקימנא בעיא שלו אפילו בראשון שלה, וקאמר: כיון דהיכא דמגופה חזיא לא תלינן בשני שלה לרבי, בכתם לא תלינן אפילו בראשון שלה:
Tosafot on Niddah 60a:16:1.english: What is [the law] regarding attributing a stain to a stain? - The Ri says that one cannot say that he was inquiring [only] about attributing [a stain] to [a woman] counting seven [clean days] who has not yet immersed, but on her first [day] it was obvious to him that she attributes [it]; for if so, why does [the Gemara] say below, "In any case, it is difficult [for Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai]"? Behold, it could have resolved [it by saying that] whether according to Rabbi or according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, the baraita is dealing with her first [day]! And furthermore, according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] as well, he should have inquired regarding her first [day], since she did not see [blood] from her body. Rather, even regarding her first [day] he inquired of him, and he resolved for him that one does not attribute [a stain to a stain] even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, but rather [only] to [a woman] who saw [blood] from her body. And now, according to all the resolutions [offered in the Gemara], it is difficult for Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai. And as for that which [the Gemara] resolves, "Both this and that are [according to] Rabbi; this is on her first [day] and that is on her second [day]" — it is the Gemara that is seeking to resolve [the baraita] in any manner that it can resolve [it], and not according to the approach of Rabbi Yehuda [bar Livai]; for behold, [Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai] said: "According to Rabbi, do not ask," and we established the dilemma posed to him as [applying] even on her first [day], and [Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai] said: Since where she saw [blood] from her body we do not attribute on her second [day] according to Rabbi, regarding a stain we do not attribute even on her first [day].

Tosafot on Niddah 60a:6:1.hebrew: תולה בשומרת יום כנגד יום - מספקא ליה להר"י אם טמא קל, כגון סופרת מקצת או הכל ולא טבלה, תולה בלא ספרה כלל, בין בנדה בין בטמא מת; ושבילי דשמעתין לא איירי אלא בטהור וטמא:
Tosafot on Niddah 60a:6:1.english: She attributes [it] to a woman who observes a day for a day - The Ri is in doubt whether one [with] a lighter impurity — such as [a woman] who counted part [of her days] or all [of them] and did not immerse — may attribute [it] to [one who] did not count at all, whether in [the case of] a niddah or in [the case of] one impure with corpse-impurity; and the paths of our sugya dealt only with a pure [person] and an impure [person].
